reading-explain-and-finding-slow-queries.r: A checkout query went from 5 ms to 4 seconds overnight. After a big import the statistics were two weeks old, so the planner expected 3 rows but found 118 000 and chose a nested loop. ANALYZE fixed it in seconds.
reading-explain-and-finding-slow-queries.x: Separate causes that look alike: a missing index shows a seq scan with many removed rows, stale statistics show a large estimate gap. Measure total cost per query, keep before and after plans, and add indexes concurrently.

indexes-that-help-and-indexes-that-hurt.r: A nightly import grew from 20 minutes to 5 hours over a year. The events table had 23 indexes totalling twice the table size. Removing thirteen unused or duplicate ones brought it under an hour.
indexes-that-help-and-indexes-that-hurt.x: Treat the index set as shared state with an owner. Review it on a schedule, remove unused and redundant indexes using statistics covering a full cycle, and prefer partial or covering indexes over broad ones.

locks-deadlocks-and-long-transactions.r: A one-line ALTER TABLE froze checkout for four minutes. It queued for a strong lock behind a long report, and every later insert queued behind it. A lock_timeout and moving the report to a replica prevented a repeat.
locks-deadlocks-and-long-transactions.x: A queued DDL statement is a hidden global lock. Always set lock_timeout and retry in quiet windows, cap idle-in-transaction and statement time, offload reports to replicas, and fix deadlocks with ordering and retry logic.

connections-pooling-and-capacity.r: After a deploy the database refused connections for ten minutes. Seventeen API pods with a pool of 10, doubled during the rolling update, hit max_connections. PgBouncer in transaction mode, smaller pools and a limited surge fixed it.
connections-pooling-and-capacity.x: Capacity is a budget: sum all pool sizes including deploy surge and batch jobs against max_connections minus reserved slots. Put a pooler in front, constrain session features, and size work_mem per workload, not globally.

replication-lag-vacuum-and-day-two-opera.r: New orders were missing for several minutes on a lagging standby, then the primary ran out of disk. An unused replication slot held 412 GB of WAL after a reporting replica was switched off. Dropping the slot freed the disk.
replication-lag-vacuum-and-day-two-opera.x: Day-two work is monitoring and discipline: lag and slot alerts, per-table autovacuum tuning, backward-compatible migrations with lock timeouts, and scheduled restore tests against RPO and RTO.

pg-stat-statements-and-query-tuning.r: A dashboard query ran 200 times a second and took only 4 ms, but it used more time than any slow report. Ranking by total time showed it, and one index cut database CPU in half.
pg-stat-statements-and-query-tuning.x: Tune by total cost, not by how scary a single query looks. The biggest win is often a cheap query called too often.

partitioning-and-data-retention.r: A nightly delete of old events ran for hours, bloated the table and blocked vacuum. Switching to monthly partitions turned retention into a drop that finished in milliseconds.
partitioning-and-data-retention.x: Retention is an operational feature. Design tables so old data can leave cheaply, and make sure queries and constraints respect the partition key.

sql-backup-and-point-in-time-recovery-op.r: A bad migration deleted a table at 14:03. Because WAL was archived, the team restored to 14:02 on a new server and exported the table, instead of losing a day of data.
sql-backup-and-point-in-time-recovery-op.x: Backups are judged by restore time and data loss, not by job success. Practice the restore until it is boring, and write down the actual numbers.

online-schema-changes-without-downtime.r: A migration added an index on a hot table without CONCURRENTLY. It waited for a lock, then blocked every write behind it for four minutes, which looked like a full outage.
online-schema-changes-without-downtime.x: Migration safety is about lock queues, not only runtime. A fast statement that waits behind a long transaction can stall everything that arrives after it.

replicas-failover-and-switchover-operati.r: After a network partition the old primary kept accepting writes while a new one was promoted. Two diverging copies of the data had to be reconciled by hand, which took days.
replicas-failover-and-switchover-operati.x: Failover is a decision about data loss and uptime. Automate it only with fencing, quorum and tested procedures, and know what it costs in lost transactions.

autovacuum-bloat-and-maintenance-windows.r: A table grew to ten times its useful size because a forgotten transaction held back cleanup for weeks. After ending it and tuning autovacuum, the table stabilized and queries recovered.
autovacuum-bloat-and-maintenance-windows.x: Vacuum is continuous maintenance, not an emergency tool. Alert on its backlog and on anything that prevents it from removing old data.

database-incident-runbook.r: Latency spiked every afternoon. The runbook found a report query holding locks and exhausting connections. Killing it and moving the report to a replica ended the incident, and the evidence made the postmortem simple.
database-incident-runbook.x: Calm, ordered checks beat clever guesses. A shared runbook lets any on-call engineer reach the same diagnosis quickly.
